desc:
Given a string s of lowercase letters, return true if s is a palindrome or can become a palindrome after deleting at most one character (at any position). Otherwise return false.

For example, "aba" gives true; "abca" gives true (delete b or c); "abc" gives false.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Trying every deletion and testing the result for being a palindrome is O(n²). Can you find out which deletions are worth trying?
Compare from both ends with two pointers. As long as the characters match, nothing needs to be deleted.
At the first mismatch s[l] != s[r], the only candidates are deleting s[l] or deleting s[r]. Check whether s[l+1..r] or s[l..r-1] is a palindrome.
editorial: Walk two pointers inward from both ends while the characters are equal. If they meet, the string is already a palindrome. At the first mismatch at positions l and r, one of the two characters has to be deleted, because every pair outside them already matches and a deletion elsewhere cannot repair this pair. So the answer is true exactly when s[l+1..r] or s[l..r-1] is a palindrome.
Each palindrome test is a plain two-pointer scan, and it happens at most twice, so the total time is O(n). The extra space is O(1) if you compare indices instead of slicing.
